data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's structural separating property is internally inconsistent and misclassifies rule 184. It claims the separator is that rules 90 and 184 are 'additive (linear over GF(2) and right-traffic-flow respectively)', but rule 184 is neither linear over GF(2) nor additive in the cellular automaton sense, so the property does not actually unify the two 'passing' rules. More seriously, the proposed property predicts rule 54 fails because it is 'nonlinear' like rule 110, but rule 54 is rule 90 XOR center (i.e., nonlinear only via the center cell). On small odd-width rings, rule 54's behavior can exactly coincide with rule 90 for states with a zero center pattern, yielding short cycles, which breaks the claimed nonlinear separator. The target also never files the required simulation artifacts returning per-(rule,width) transient and cycle-length tables, instead asserting a summary witness ('isolated 1' for W=11) without the sandboxed enumeration the problem requires.
